meta.name: The World, 1914
meta.description: The whole world at the start of 1914, from the Arctic to Cape Horn: the European great powers and their empires, the United States and Japan, China two years into its republic, and the independent kingdoms of Asia and Africa. The alliances of 1914 are in force, with the Anglo-Japanese Alliance and the dominions beside Britain, and the claims of the time stand. Historical borders, approximated from present-day divisions; colonies and protectorates are held by the powers that governed them, and realms too small for a province on this scale are drawn with a neighbour.
meta.blurb: A huge historical campaign: about 1,600 provinces and 57 realms on the eve of the Great War.
meta.style: Empires across oceans; every front at once
attribution: Coastlines, lakes, rivers, first-level divisions and towns: Natural Earth (naturalearthdata.com), public domain.

Borders of 1914 approximated from present-day divisions; historical names, town populations of about 1914, ridges, passes and straits are authored (tools/earth.data.ts, with tools/europe.data.ts for Europe). Arms are simplified, in national colours.

nations.name: United Kingdom
nations.summary: The empire on which the sun never sets: the British Isles, India, Egypt and the Sudan, half of Africa, Malaya and the Caribbean, held together by the largest navy and merchant fleet in the world.
nations.strength: Sea power and commerce: trade pays more and fleets are cheap to keep.
nations.constraint: A small army for the largest empire, spread over every continent.

nations.name: French Republic
nations.summary: The Third Republic, with a conscript army along its eastern fortress line and the second colonial empire: North and West Africa, Madagascar and Indochina.
nations.strength: Fortress belt and a large reserve: forts cost less.
nations.constraint: A low birth rate: men are precious.

nations.name: German Empire
nations.summary: The industrial empire at the centre of Europe, with the strongest army on the continent, a fleet built to rival Britain’s and colonies in Africa and the Pacific. Luxembourg, in its customs union, is drawn with it.
nations.strength: Industry and staff work: research and income above every neighbour.
nations.constraint: Two fronts: France in the west, Russia in the east.

nations.name: Austria-Hungary
nations.summary: The Dual Monarchy of the Habsburgs: a dozen peoples from Bohemia to Bosnia under one crown, newly anxious about Serbia.
nations.strength: Mountain fortresses and a large army on paper.
nations.constraint: Many peoples: newly held land integrates slowly and unrest runs high.

nations.name: Russian Empire
nations.summary: The empire of the tsars from Poland to the Pacific: Finland, the Caucasus, Turkestan and Siberia, slow to mobilise and vast in manpower.
nations.strength: Vast manpower: armies are cheap to fill.
nations.constraint: Railways and industry lag, and the distances are immense: research and supply are slow.

nations.name: Kingdom of Italy
nations.summary: A young kingdom, newly master of Libya and the Dodecanese, with Eritrea and Somaliland on the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean.
nations.strength: A long coast and a growing fleet.
nations.constraint: Poor in coal and iron, and torn between alliances.

nations.name: Ottoman Empire
nations.summary: The old empire of the straits, shrunk by the Balkan wars, still ruling Anatolia, the Levant, Mesopotamia, the Hejaz and the Yemen from Constantinople.
nations.strength: The straits and a large hinterland: defenders fight well at home.
nations.constraint: Debts and distances: income and supply are weak, and the provinces restless.

nations.name: Kingdom of Spain
nations.summary: A kingdom behind the Pyrenees, neutral and recovering from the loss of Cuba and the Philippines, with a zone in northern Morocco, Río de Oro and Spanish Guinea.
nations.strength: Mountains and a long border to defend: forts are cheap.

nations.name: Portuguese Republic
nations.summary: An Atlantic republic since 1910, Britain’s oldest ally, holding Angola, Mozambique, Guinea and Timor.
nations.strength: Atlantic trade.
nations.constraint: Small, poor and far from the rest of Europe.

nations.name: Kingdom of the Netherlands
nations.summary: A rich trading kingdom of ports and polders, neutral between Britain and Germany, and master of the East Indies.
nations.strength: Commerce and the spice islands: trade and income above its size.
nations.constraint: Small and flat, between two great powers.

nations.name: Kingdom of Belgium
nations.summary: An industrial kingdom whose neutrality the great powers guarantee, ruling the vast Congo since 1908.
nations.strength: Coal and factories, and a guaranteed neutrality.
nations.constraint: On the road between France and Germany.

nations.name: Swiss Confederation
nations.summary: The armed neutral confederation of the Alpine cantons.
nations.strength: Mountain defence: militia and forts hold the passes.

nations.name: Kingdom of Denmark
nations.summary: A farming kingdom at the Baltic straits, with Iceland, the Faroes and Greenland across the North Atlantic.
nations.strength: Dairy and trade: income above its size.

nations.name: Kingdom of Sweden
nations.summary: A long kingdom of forest, ore and timber, neutral and well armed.
nations.strength: Iron ore: industry starts cheaply.

nations.name: Kingdom of Norway
nations.summary: Independent since 1905: a seafaring kingdom of fjords whose merchant fleet sails every sea.
nations.strength: Shipping: trade pays more and straits cost less to cross.

nations.name: Kingdom of Romania
nations.summary: A kingdom on the lower Danube with the Ploiești oil fields, newly enlarged by Southern Dobruja and courted by both camps.
nations.strength: Oil and grain.

nations.name: Kingdom of Bulgaria
nations.summary: Beaten in the Second Balkan War of 1913, but holding Western Thrace and an outlet to the Aegean.
nations.strength: A hard army: soldiers fight well.
nations.constraint: Isolated, and its neighbours hold what it claims.

nations.name: Kingdom of Serbia
nations.summary: A kingdom doubled by the Balkan wars, battle-hardened and facing Austria-Hungary across the Danube; Montenegro, its ally and kin, is drawn with it.
nations.strength: Veterans: soldiers fight well, and hills help them.
nations.constraint: Landlocked and exhausted by two wars.

nations.name: Kingdom of Greece
nations.summary: A maritime kingdom enlarged by the Balkan wars with Macedonia, Epirus, Crete and the Aegean islands.
nations.strength: Islands and ships.

nations.name: Principality of Albania
nations.summary: Independent since 1912 and given a foreign prince in 1914: a mountain state its neighbours covet.
nations.strength: Mountains.
nations.constraint: A new state with little administration: land integrates slowly.

nations.name: Sublime State of Persia
nations.summary: The Qajar shah’s realm from the Caspian to the Gulf, divided into Russian and British zones of influence, with the oil of the south newly in British hands.
nations.strength: Distance and mountains.
nations.constraint: Weak and penetrated by foreign powers: income and research are low.

nations.name: Emirate of Afghanistan
nations.summary: The mountain emirate between the Russian and British empires, which conducts its foreign affairs through India.
nations.strength: Mountains and hardy tribes: soldiers fight well at home.

nations.name: Emirate of Najd and Hasa
nations.summary: Ibn Saud’s desert emirate of central Arabia, newly master of the Gulf coast of Hasa and rival of the Rashidis of Ha’il.
nations.strength: Desert warriors: cavalry strikes hard.
nations.constraint: Sand and few people: no industry, little income.

nations.name: Sultanate of Muscat and Oman
nations.summary: A seafaring sultanate at the mouth of the Gulf, under British protection, at odds with the imamate of its interior.
nations.strength: Dhows and the Indian Ocean trade.

nations.name: Kingdom of Nepal
nations.summary: A Himalayan kingdom ruled by the Rana prime ministers, closed to foreigners and a friend of British India.
nations.strength: Gurkha soldiers and mountain walls.

nations.name: Republic of China
nations.summary: The young republic of Yuan Shikai, three years after the fall of the Qing: the most populous country on earth, with foreign concessions in its ports.
nations.strength: Numbers: an immense population and manpower.
nations.constraint: Divided provinces and foreign debt: income, research and integration are weak.

nations.name: Tibet
nations.summary: The Dalai Lama’s state on the roof of the world, independent in fact since the Chinese garrison left in 1913.
nations.strength: The highest mountains on earth.

nations.name: Bogd Khanate of Mongolia
nations.summary: Outer Mongolia under the Bogd Khan, independent of China since 1911 and leaning on Russia.
nations.strength: Horsemen of the steppe.
nations.constraint: Empty land: little income or industry.

nations.name: Empire of Japan
nations.summary: The island empire that defeated Russia in 1905, ruling Korea and Formosa and allied to Britain, with a modern navy and a growing industry.
nations.strength: Discipline and a modern fleet: soldiers fight well and research is quick.

nations.name: Kingdom of Siam
nations.summary: The only kingdom of South-East Asia to keep its independence, a buffer between British Burma and French Indochina.
nations.strength: Diplomacy between the empires: others think well of it.

nations.name: Ethiopian Empire
nations.summary: The ancient highland empire that beat Italy at Adwa in 1896, independent among the African colonies.
nations.strength: Highland armies: defenders fight well at home.

nations.name: Republic of Liberia
nations.summary: A small republic on the Grain Coast, independent since 1847 and indebted to American and European banks.
nations.strength: American friendship: others think well of it.

nations.name: Union of South Africa
nations.summary: The dominion of 1910 joining the Cape, Natal, the Transvaal and the Orange Free State, rich in gold and diamonds.
nations.strength: Gold and diamonds: income above its size.
nations.constraint: A divided white minority ruling a black majority.

nations.name: United States of America
nations.summary: The largest industrial economy in the world, between two oceans, with the Philippines, Hawaii and Puerto Rico, the Panama Canal about to open and a small army.
nations.strength: Industry and capital: income and research above everyone.
nations.constraint: A small standing army and a public wary of foreign wars.

nations.name: Dominion of Canada
nations.summary: A self-governing dominion of the British Empire from the Atlantic to the Pacific, its prairies filling with settlers.
nations.strength: Wheat, timber and rail: trade pays well.
nations.constraint: Few people for an immense land.

nations.name: United Mexican States
nations.summary: A republic in the middle of its revolution, with Huerta in the capital, Carranza, Villa and Zapata in the field and American marines in Veracruz.
nations.strength: Silver and oil.
nations.constraint: Civil war: the provinces are restless and slow to integrate.

nations.name: Republic of Guatemala
nations.summary: The largest of the Central American republics, under the long dictatorship of Estrada Cabrera.
nations.strength: Coffee and highland forts.

nations.name: Republic of Honduras
nations.summary: A republic of banana coasts and mountain towns, where the fruit companies make and unmake governments.
nations.strength: Bananas: the fruit trade pays.

nations.name: Republic of El Salvador
nations.summary: The smallest and most crowded of the Central American republics, a land of coffee and volcanoes.
nations.strength: Coffee and a dense population.

nations.name: Republic of Nicaragua
nations.summary: A republic of lakes and volcanoes under American marines since 1912, coveted for a second canal.
nations.strength: The lakes and a canal route.

nations.name: Republic of Costa Rica
nations.summary: A peaceful coffee republic with more teachers than soldiers.
nations.strength: Schools and stability: research and opinion are good.

nations.name: Republic of Panama
nations.summary: The isthmus republic of 1903, whose canal opens to shipping in August 1914 under American control.
nations.strength: The canal: trade pays and straits are cheap.

nations.name: Republic of Cuba
nations.summary: An island republic of sugar, independent since 1902 under the eye of the United States.
nations.strength: Sugar: trade and income.

nations.name: Republic of Haiti
nations.summary: The first black republic, proud and unstable, with five presidents between 1911 and 1915.
nations.strength: Mountains and a fierce independence.

nations.name: Dominican Republic
nations.summary: The eastern republic of Hispaniola, whose customs houses American agents have run since 1905.
nations.strength: Sugar and cacao.

nations.name: Republic of Colombia
nations.summary: An Andean republic of coffee and mountains, still resentful of the loss of Panama.
nations.strength: Mountain valleys: forts are cheap.

nations.name: United States of Venezuela
nations.summary: The republic of Gómez, cattle plains and the first oil wells on Lake Maracaibo.
nations.strength: Oil beneath the lake.

nations.name: Republic of Ecuador
nations.summary: The republic on the equator, between the cacao coast and the volcanoes of the Andes.
nations.strength: Cacao and the high valleys.

nations.name: Republic of Peru
nations.summary: The old viceroyalty of the Andes, still claiming Tacna and Arica lost to Chile in the Pacific War.
nations.strength: Guano, copper and the mountain wall.
nations.constraint: Defeat in the last war and a long frontier.

nations.name: United States of Brazil
nations.summary: The giant of South America, a federal republic of coffee and rubber reaching deep into the Amazon.
nations.strength: Coffee and rubber: trade pays well.
nations.constraint: Vast and thinly settled: supply is slow.

nations.name: Republic of Bolivia
nations.summary: A landlocked republic of the high Andes, rich in tin and silver, its coast lost to Chile.
nations.strength: Tin and silver.

nations.name: Republic of Paraguay
nations.summary: A small river republic still recovering from the catastrophe of 1864–70, claiming the Chaco.
nations.strength: A hard people.

nations.name: Oriental Republic of Uruguay
nations.summary: A small, prosperous republic of cattle and reforms on the River Plate.
nations.strength: Beef and wool: income above its size.

nations.name: Argentine Republic
nations.summary: One of the richest countries in the world, exporting wheat and beef from the Pampas through Buenos Aires.
nations.strength: Grain and beef: trade and income.
nations.constraint: Its wealth depends on British markets and ships.

nations.name: Republic of Chile
nations.summary: The long republic of the Pacific coast, victorious in the nitrate war, with a strong navy and the Atacama’s saltpetre.
nations.strength: Nitrates and a Prussian-trained army.

nations.name: Commonwealth of Australia
nations.summary: A federation of six colonies since 1901, a continent of wool and gold with five million people, governing Papua.
nations.strength: Wool and gold: trade pays well.
nations.constraint: An empty continent far from everyone.

nations.name: Dominion of New Zealand
nations.summary: The southernmost dominion, a land of sheep and dairies loyal to Britain.
nations.strength: Wool and butter.
